candidates.title: EmoHarness: Boosting Multimodal Emotion Understanding with Meta-Harness Evolving
candidates.content: Small multimodal models can misjudge emotion when words, voice, and visual cues conflict. We present EmoHarness, which runs such a model, the frozen student, inside a harness: the prompts, settings, and verification code around its calls. A human-written starting harness, the scaffold, numbers the student's visual observations, transcript, and prosody descriptions as citable evidence and has the student weigh candidate emotions against it. In Meta-Harness Evolving (MHE), a stronger LLM, the Builder, reads the student's errors and execution traces offline and edits the harness; static checks and validation gates decide which edits are kept, and the Builder never sees evaluation items. On 5,507 MME-Emotion items, EmoHarness raises task-macro Recognition by 7.6-13.4 points over a single video-only call for all four students and both Builders. Transcripts and prosody descriptions supply most of this boost (+5.38 to +10.71); the scaffold changes the audio-augmented call by -0.79 to +2.54, partly through extra multi-label predictions, and evolved edits add at most +0.95, although no evolved increment survives Holm correction. candidates.title: MotionGraphicsBench: Evaluating Motion Graphics Generation with Programmatic Verification
candidates.content: Large language models can generate motion graphics from static images and natural language requests, but it remains difficult to evaluate how well models can follow requests that combine spatial, appearance, and temporal requirements. We introduce MotionGraphicsBench, an expert-curated benchmark of 100 instances for animating an input static SVG with a motion edit prompt. By supplying all required visual elements, our editing task reflects a designer-like workflow and isolates motion generation from graphic generation. Derived from real-world Lottie motion designs, our benchmark contains diverse combinations of spatio-temporal animation behaviors. Each benchmark instance pairs its model input with a deterministic, human-readable verification program that accepts different valid implementations and reports which prompt requirements pass or fail, rather than comparing against a reference animation or using a VLM judge. We construct these programs with a multi-agent pipeline using human-labeled animations and synthesized test cases. On a balanced test set of 180 animations, our programs achieve 93.3% raw agreement with human judgments, compared with 83.3% for a GPT-6 Astra VLM baselin

candidates.title: RidgeFill: Training-Free Late-Layer Cache Fill for Faster Prefill
candidates.content: RidgeFill shortens prefill by not computing most of a model's upper layers for the prompt. The lower layers run exactly up to a split; from the split layer's state a per-layer map predicts every later layer's input, and each late layer writes its cache from that prediction. The design follows YOCO and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, where the projection is trained into the model. RidgeFill retrofits it onto models that were never trained for it: the map is a ridge regression fitted once in closed form from one pass over calibration text, the layer's own projections run unchanged, and a chosen set of rows, the last few thousand tokens, and every decoding step run the full model. Nothing is trained and no token is dropped. Most of the work was in measurement, finding a repeatable methodology. Loss averaged over all tokens hides RidgeFill's error. Needle retrieval in the filled region, loss on tokens that depend on distant context, and splice tests that swap filled keys or values for exact ones show which component carries it: the keys on Llama-3.1-8B, half of it in their scale, and the values and the recurrent state on Qwen3.5-9B. candidates.title: Archaeal histones coordinate conserved DNA sequence motifs to promote CRISPR adaptive immunity
candidates.content: Abstract Archaea and bacteria acquire resistance to viruses by integrating fragments of foreign DNA at the beginning of a CRISPR locus. In the archaeon Pyrococcus furiosus , histones bind the leader to promote specific integration at the first CRISPR repeat. However, it remains unknown whether archaeal CRISPR leaders contain conserved DNA sequence motifs required for integration. Here, we analyze 542 archaeal CRISPR leaders found across Thermococcales and Methanococcales . We identify 36 motifs found up to 500 bps upstream of archaeal CRISPR loci. Scrambling or truncating novel motifs or histone binding sites found 100–400 bps upstream of the P. furiosus CRISPR modestly decreases integration efficiency. However, mutation of motif T2, which overlaps with the proximal histone site and is adjacent to the CRISPR, ablates both histone-mediated and histone-independent integration. Mutations tiled across T2 reveal that a pyrimidine at position −3 of the leader is required for histone-independent integration, and basepairs −4 to −19 are required for histone-mediated integration. candidates.title: Cell-free expression and NGS-powered substrate profiling reveal a thermostable metagenomic meganuclease from an extreme environment with novel specificity
candidates.content: Abstract As an alternative to historical enzyme isolation, metagenomic databases (e.g. MGnify) provide information on vast unculturable microbial diversity, including extreme environments, and constitute an enormous source of functional proteins. Conservative mining of these data by close sequence homology alone tends to identify merely different versions of known enzymes. Here we present a discovery strategy for meganucleases based on wider capture of less homologous enzymes in metagenomic databases, and incorporating metadata with their homology. We use cell-free expression to bypass host incompatibility and the need for purification, along with deep sequencing for experimental assessment of substrate specificity and cleavage pattern, thereby circumventing classical gel-based profiling. Specifically, we discovered the temperature-stable (>55°C), intron-encoded LAGLIDADG meganuclease I-MG11 that recognizes a GC-rich 17 base pair sequence to generate 4-nt palindromic 3′-overhangs—the first monomeric meganuclease to produce such overhangs. candidates.title: Transcription factor 3 cooperates with CXXC finger protein 1 to regulate histone H3K4 trimethylation and developmental competence in mouse oocytes
candidates.content: Abstract During oogenesis, the establishment of oocyte-specific gene expression relies on epigenetic and transcriptional remodeling. Both histone modifications and transcription factors are crucial for the oocyte to acquire developmental competence; however, the mechanisms involved remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify transcription factor 3 (TCF3), an E-protein family member, as a key maternal regulator of oocyte developmental potential. Oocyte-specific deletion of Tcf3 results in female infertility, characterized by impaired meiotic maturation and early embryonic arrest at the two-cell stage. These defects are associated with defective maternal mRNA clearance and disrupted establishment of the H3K4me3 landscape in maturing oocytes. Mechanistically, we demonstrate that TCF3 directs H3K4me3 deposition at target gene promoters through interaction with CXXC finger protein 1 (CXXC1), the core subunit of the SETD1 histone methyltransferase complex. Importantly, this TCF3–CXXC1 interaction depends on their DNA-binding activity, highlighting the specificity of TCF3 in coordinating with CXXC1 to regulate maternal target genes, such as Pabpn1l . candidates.content: Background: Conventional cancer therapies are heavily constrained by systemic toxicity, off-target side effects, and poor deep-tissue penetration due to the highly heterogeneous tumor microenvironment (TME). Although gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) possess exceptional localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) properties ideal for photothermal therapy (PTT), their clinical translation is bottlenecked by inconsistent passive accumulation and chemical toxicity arising from conventional synthetic surfactants. Objective: This study developed a sustainable, biocompatible bio-hybrid platform utilizing the probiotic Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 (EcN) as an autonomous, tumor-homing living carrier integrated with AuNPs synthesized via an eco-friendly intracellular green chemistry approach. Methods: EcN cultures were prepared in Luria-Bertani (LB) medium and subsequently exposed to a 1 mM chloroauric acid (HAuCl4) metallic precursor. A facile, room-temperature green synthesis protocol was established by utilizing ascorbic acid (Vitamin C) as a non-toxic co-reductant to drive a seed-mediated crystallization onto intra-bacterial metallic seeds. candidates.title: Allele-selective targeting of uromodulin by antisense oligonucleotides reduces aggregates and kidney damage in a mouse model of autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease
candidates.content: Abstract Autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease (ADTKD) arises from gain-of-toxic-function mutations in the UMOD gene coding for uromodulin, the most abundant protein excreted in normal urine. Mutant uromodulin accumulates in the cells lining the thick ascending limb (TAL) of the loop of Henle, leading to intracellular aggregates, cellular stress, and kidney damage. Here, we demonstrate that an antisense gapmer oligonucleotide (ASO) designed against the representative c.553C > A (p.R185S) UMOD mutation produced allele-selective silencing of the mutant messenger RNA and protein in kidney cells. Short-term administration of a murine ASO analogue in the established Umod R186S/+ mouse model of ADTKD suppressed uromodulin and lowered tubular damage, whereas a non-targeting scrambled control was inactive. After a 4-week treatment, ASO accumulation in the Umod R186S/+ kidneys reached ∼320 000 copies per TAL cell, quantified using a sensitive splint-ligation assay. The ASO treatment suppressed premature mutant uromodulin and its toxic aggregates in Umod R186S/+ kidneys, whereas it had no effects on wild-type uromodulin in Umod +/+ kidneys. Notably, the ASO improved tubular fu

candidates.title: The anti-phage defense system GAPS4 is a double-edged sword that sensitizes bacteria to DNA-damaging agents
candidates.content: Abstract The arms race between bacteria and bacteriophages (phages) gave rise to multiple layers of antagonistic mechanisms, many of which remain unexplored. Here, we investigated the widespread anti-phage defense system GAPS4. We found that GAPS4 forms a heterotetrameric complex containing active PD-(D/E)xK phosphodiesterase domains. It is triggered upon sensing DNA damage, leading to genomic DNA degradation and cell suicide. We further demonstrated that this activation mechanism renders GAPS4 a double-edged sword, sensitizing bacteria to various DNA-targeting antibacterial agents. Collectively, our findings reveal a possible evolutionary trade-off between anti-phage defense and immunity against interbacterial antagonism.

candidates.title: Longtail-SWE: High-Quality SWE Tasks for Underrepresented Languages
candidates.content: Challenging repository-level benchmarks remain limited for many programming language ecosystems, where filtering scarce candidates with ambiguous descriptions or defective tests can discard valuable engineering problems. We introduce Longtail-SWE, a benchmark of 202 issue-resolution tasks across 13 languages with limited coverage in existing repository-level benchmarks: Clojure, Dart, Elixir, Erlang, F#, Haskell, Julia, Kotlin, Lua, OCaml, R, Scala, and Swift. Its construction uses a solver--judge--repairer pipeline: a solver attempts each candidate task, and a judge reviews the task together with the solver's trajectory and test results to guide revisions to tests and task descriptions. These revisions aim to correct tests that reject valid alternative implementations or accept incorrect solutions while retaining challenging tasks and preserving their intended requirements. We evaluate nine model configurations, including frontier models, and analyze task-solving performance, consistency across repeated attempts, and resource usage. candidates.title: System Prompts Affect Response Bias More Than Discriminability in LLM Safety
candidates.content: arXiv:2611.11074v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language model safety evaluations often focus on a compliance-refusal tradeoff: models should refuse unsafe requests without refusing safe ones. We argue that this misses a broader form of prompt-conditioned task selection, where the same request can elicit different behaviors depending on the system prompt. We investigate this using a controlled evaluation crossing eight safety-task prompt families with three clarity levels across HarmBench, XSTest, and IHEval. Holding benchmark items fixed, we evaluate 13 models and use signal detection theory to distinguish two possibilities: whether models become better at telling safe from unsafe requests (discriminability), or simply more willing to refuse (response criterion). We find substantial differences in discriminability across models, but system prompts primarily shift the willingness to refuse, with smaller and less consistent effects on discriminability. Increasing prompt clarity makes models more willing to refuse without reliably improving their ability to distinguish safe from unsafe requests. candidates.title: TS-GEAR: Taobao Shangou GEnerative Ad Retrieval
candidates.content: arXiv:2611.12180v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: On-demand delivery platforms such as DoorDash and Uber Eats impose a constraint absent in traditional e-commerce: merchants beyond the user's delivery range are invalid candidates rather than merely low-ranked. Generative retrieval has recently shown strong potential in large-scale retrieval systems. Adapting it to this setting, however, poses three challenges. First, existing semantic IDs encode geography only as a soft signal, so reachability can only rely on a non-differentiable post-generation hard truncation. Second, user preferences vary substantially across both regions and queries, so aggregating historical behaviors without conditioning on geography and the current query yields biased interest estimates. Third, the retrieved candidate set is evaluated by its collective value, yet autoregressive training scores each sequence independently, with no set-level signal to discourage redundant near-duplicates. candidates.title: PolicyGuide: From Guarding One Action to Guiding the Whole Workflow for Policy-Compliant LLM Agents
candidates.content: arXiv:2608.19861v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Customer-service LLM agents must follow organizational policy when acting on a user's behalf. Compliance failures arise from either forbidden actions, such as granting an ineligible change, or omitted procedural requirements, such as identification or confirmation. Runtime safeguards can intervene on risky actions, but action-local checks do not guide an agent through a multi-step procedure. Workflow-following systems support prescribed process execution, but primarily target workflow completion rather than safeguarding agent behavior. PolicyGuide instead compiles each domain policy into a workflow graph and invokes a proactive verifier at user-turn boundaries. From persisted graph state, the verifier reconciles open requests and returns step-specific remediation along a policy-compliant path. Across the $\tau^2$-bench airline, retail, and telecom domains with a GPT 5.4 agent and verifier, PolicyGuide raises mean $\mathrm{Pass}^4$ from $0.42$ to $0.62$, with the largest gain on telecom ($0.19$ to $0.61$), the most workflow-structured domain.
